source.title: Loss Spike in Training Neural Networks
source.authors: Xiaolong Li; Z. Xu; Zhongwang Zhang

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices; no apparent cutoff.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own experiments on gradient-descent training dynamics and loss spikes, including CIFAR-10 subsets. Those results relate to learning-rate stability and training behavior, but do not test the listed versions’ classification-error claims in the stated benchmark settings.
record.gate_note: The paper reports loss-spike, Hessian-eigenvalue, frequency, and condensation outcomes. These do not measure training classification error as V1–V4 describe, two-layer teacher-student spurious minima (V2), BN versus shortcut effects on training error (V3), initialization comparisons in V4, or training recovering above a stated stability limit in wide squared-loss networks/full-batch sharpness dynamics in V5. Its BN VGG-11 figures also do not compare BN with no BN or Fixup, so they do not test V6. The experiments with a CIFAR-10 subset use 1,000 images and MSE; the CIFAR10-2k setup is used for batch-size generalization comparisons.
record.test_reason: The study's own gradient-descent loss and Hessian trajectories test V5's edge-of-stability component. Section 3.1 explicitly places the Figure 2 loss spikes at the edge of stability; Section 3.2 reports loss increasing above 2/η and decreasing after sharpness falls below it. Requiring classification error, or requiring every V5 experiment to start above the initial stability limit, incorrectly excludes these results.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors explain spike ascent through a lower-loss-as-sharper landscape and rapid descent through predominantly low-frequency output changes. They argue that maximum Hessian eigenvalue indicates linear stability but does not directly characterize generalization. Their experiments associate loss spikes with feature condensation and flatter solutions; the mechanism and generalization implications remain open.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes full-batch gradient-descent training dynamics, Hessian sharpness, frequency content, and condensation in fitting tasks and CIFAR-10 subsets. It does not use the versions’ classification-error, bad-minimum, shortcut, initialization-comparison, stability-recovery, or normalization-comparison recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Learning rate changes spike occurrence and the observed condensation/sharpness trends. Initialization regime changes the relationship: in the condensed regime, Appendix B.1 reports that condensed variance and λmax do not display similar trends at early training.

fits_no_version.finding: Loss spikes accompany increased parameter condensation; condensation and sharpness often have similar trends, with an early-training exception under condensed initialization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Loss spikes can accompany feature condensation, and the sharpness–condensation relationship depends on initialization and training stage.

fits_no_version.finding: Training/test solutions and different-batch-size solutions differ little along the largest-eigenvalue directions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Maximum Hessian eigenvalue alone does not directly characterize generalization in these experiments.

record.peer_reviewed: Journal of Computational Mathematics (venue stated; article text identifies itself as a preprint)
record.problems: The paper reports no numerical training classification-error results relevant to the claim versions. Many outcomes are conveyed in figures without tabulated values. Several experiments use synthetic one-dimensional fitting rather than classification benchmarks. The paper notes that the condensed-regime early-training trends do not match the linear-regime trends. No uncertainty estimates are stated for the reported comparisons except the random-output error bar in Fig. 4, which is not relevant to the listed versions.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible claim-version results were omitted. Figure 4’s frequency proportions and Figure 5–6’s generalization geometry outcomes are not recorded as rows because they do not test behavior named by any version; the related CIFAR-10 geometry results are summarized in R4–R6 as findings about the claim subject.

untested.parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted labels, model-size comparisons, and regularized or early-stopped recipes.
Teacher–student spurious-minimum frequencies and the effect of adding student neurons.
Depth degradation, residual-shortcut comparisons, deep plain tanh training, and Fixup.
Activation-matched initialization comparisons, signal or gradient preservation, training speed, and trainable depth.

A learning-rate sweep calibrated to the initial linearized stability limit in wide squared-loss networks; the boundary between recovery and divergence; and divergence from initially subthreshold runs. The observed later-training spikes do not establish these components.
Batch normalization versus no normalization for training speed or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

missing.what: Width-20 tanh FNN loss and Hessian trajectories showing a late-training loss spike, crossing of 2/η = 40, and recovery. This is an additional model setting testing V5.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source listed for V5. Its later-training edge-of-stability results qualify as tests independently of whether it reproduces the initial catapult experiment. Unmeasured initial-threshold and divergence components warrant no scope-limiting verdict.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report training classification error for sufficiently large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, or smaller/regularized models.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student problem or student-width sweep measuring spurious-minimum frequency.
Does not compare plain and residual networks’ training errors by depth, nor test the cited deep tanh or Fixup recipes.
Does not compare activation-matched, Gaussian, or orthogonal initializations for training speed or trainable depth.

Although it studies loss spikes and Hessian sharpness, it does not test recovery above the initial linearized stability limit in wide squared-loss networks or sharpness hovering at the threshold during full-batch training. It does not report the cited below-threshold divergence comparison.
Does not compare batch normalization against no normalization for speed or learning-rate tolerance, or test Fixup.

rows.subject: Two-layer ReLU CNN with Max Pooling
rows.operation_detail: Full-batch gradient descent with MSE on the first 1,000 CIFAR-10 training images; the reported training trajectory has a loss spike.
rows.measure: Training loss and maximum Hessian eigenvalue over epochs; no classification error reported.
rows.value: Loss spikes; λmax exceeds 2/η during the ascent and drops below 2/η during the descent, as described for the experiments.
rows.note: This is a training-dynamics outcome, not a training classification-error measure.
rows.check: The loss and Hessian trajectories directly bear on V5's edge-of-stability component. The comparison is with the instantaneous threshold 2/η = 20, rather than an initial-sharpness threshold. No classification-error measure is needed for V5.

rows.subject: VGG-11 with batch normalization
rows.operation_detail: Train on CIFAR-10 and report loss-spike dynamics at learning rate 0.2.
rows.measure: Training loss and maximum Hessian eigenvalue over epochs; no classification error reported.
rows.value: Loss spike is shown in the figure; the text states that typical loss spikes occur when λmax exceeds 2/η and loss increases, and loss decreases when λmax < 2/η.
rows.note: The VGG learning-rate condition is shown in the figure; the text describes loss-spike behavior generally but does not separately state a value for this condition.
rows.check: Figure 2(g) supplies an own-result edge-of-stability trajectory, with threshold 2/η = 10. Section 3.1 specifies a CIFAR-10 subset of 1,024 examples; the row omits this restriction. The VGG loss function is not specified in the supplied setup.

rows.subject: VGG-11 with batch normalization
rows.operation_detail: Train on CIFAR-10 and report loss-spike dynamics at learning rate 0.3; PCA analysis is also performed on spikes from this run.
rows.measure: Training loss and maximum Hessian eigenvalue over epochs; no classification error reported.
rows.value: Loss spike is shown; the text states that λmax above 2/η is associated with loss increase and λmax below 2/η with loss decrease in the described spike experiments.
rows.note: The text specifies that PCA analysis uses the 0.3 run but does not separately quantify its training error.
rows.check: Figure 2(h–i) supplies an own-result edge-of-stability trajectory and recovery through a flatter region, with threshold 2/η approximately 6.67. Section 3.1 specifies 1,024 CIFAR-10 examples. The VGG loss function is not specified.

rows.subject: Two-layer ReLU CNN with Max Pooling
rows.size_stated: Architecture described as three-layer CNN; 16 convolution kernels in Table 1
rows.operation_detail: Compare parameter differences between a model trained on the training set and a model further trained on the test set along Hessian eigendirections.
rows.measure: Projection of θtest − θtrain on each eigendirection of H(θtrain); no training classification error reported.
rows.value: The text states projections are positively correlated with eigenvalue index, and θtrain and θtest have little difference on low-frequency part.
rows.note: A parameter-geometry/generalization comparison, not one of the listed training-error outcomes.
rows.check: Parameter differences across training and test solutions do not measure any version. The architecture has one convolutional layer and one linear layer; Table 1's three-layer title conflicts with the two-layer description in Figure 6.

rows.subject: Three-layer ReLU CNN with Max Pooling
rows.size_stated: Architecture described as three-layer CNN; 16 and 32 convolution kernels in Table 2
rows.operation_detail: Compare parameter differences between a model trained on the training set and a model further trained on the test set along Hessian eigendirections.
rows.measure: Projection of θtest − θtrain on each eigendirection of H(θtrain); no training classification error reported.
rows.value: The text states projections are positively correlated with eigenvalue index, and θtrain and θtest have little difference on low-frequency part.
rows.note: The training-set/test-set parameter comparison does not measure the training-error behavior in the versions.
rows.check: Generalization geometry does not measure any version; using Xavier initialization alone does not test V4.

rows.subject: Five-layer ReLU CNN with Max Pooling
rows.operation_detail: Compare minima found using small and large batch sizes along Hessian eigendirections.
rows.measure: Projection of θlarge − θsmall on each eigendirection of H(θtrain); no training classification error reported.
rows.value: The text states the two minima have little difference in eigendirections corresponding to the largest s eigenvalues when the explained-variance ratio is close to 1.
rows.note: This result concerns parameter differences between batch-size minima and generalization, not the listed training-error claims.
rows.check: Differences between batch-size solutions do not measure any version. This is not a width sweep or a measurement of spurious-minimum frequency.

rows.subject: Two-layer ReLU FNN
rows.operation_detail: Full-batch gradient descent with MSE, comparing a large learning rate with a small learning rate from identical initialization.

conditions.value: η = 2 × 10−2 (large) versus η = 6 × 10−2 (as printed in the figure)
same initialization across runs; θ ∼ N(0, m−0.8) stated for Fig. 12

rows.measure: Loss trajectory and parameter feature-direction/amplitude distribution; no classification error.
rows.baseline: Small learning-rate run: loss without a significant spike.
rows.value: Large learning-rate run: significant loss spike; the text says non-zero parameters tend to condense in several discrete orientations.
rows.note: Figure labels appear to conflict with the discussion's stated example of η = 0.03 and 0.05; row preserves figure values as printed and records the setup text in note.
rows.check: The recorded loss-spike and condensation comparison does not establish a stability-threshold crossing. The learning-rate assignment is reversed: Figure 8(a) identifies 0.02 as the small rate and 0.06 as the large rate. Appendix A's paragraph explicitly concerns Figure 12 and cannot establish Figure 8(a)'s initialization.

rows.subject: Two-layer tanh FNN
rows.size_stated: 100 hidden neurons in Section 5; 200 hidden neurons in Experimental setups for Fig. 8(b)
rows.operation_detail: Full-batch gradient descent with MSE, comparing a large learning rate with a small learning rate from identical initialization.
rows.measure: Loss trajectory, output, and parameter feature distribution; no classification error.
rows.baseline: Small learning-rate run: no loss spike and parameters closer to initialization.
rows.value: Large learning-rate run: loss spike; text says non-zero parameters tend to condense in several discrete orientations.
rows.note: The main text says 100 hidden neurons, while the setup for Fig. 8(b) says width 200.
rows.check: The comparison measures loss spikes and condensation without establishing the stability threshold. Preserve the unresolved width discrepancy: Section 5.1 says 100, whereas Appendix A says 200.

rows.subject: ReLU neural network
rows.operation_detail: Vary learning rate and measure end-of-training condensed variance and maximum Hessian eigenvalue.
rows.measure: Condensed variance and λmax at end of training; loss-spike threshold indicated experimentally.
rows.value: Text states condensed variance decreases as learning rate increases, λmax exhibits a decreasing trend, and learning rates above the marked threshold produce observed loss spikes.
rows.note: This reports a correlation between sharpness and condensation, not classification error or the stability-limit recovery in V5.
rows.check: Terminal sharpness and condensation versus learning rate do not establish recovery above the initial stability limit or sharpness hovering during continued loss reduction. The empirical spike threshold is not identified as the initial linearized stability limit.

rows.subject: ReLU neural network
rows.operation_detail: Track condensed variance and λmax over early training at learning rate 0.03.
rows.measure: Time course of condensed variance and λmax; whether loss spikes occur.
rows.value: No loss spike; text states λmax and condensed variance show the same trend and both decrease during the same epoch, ignoring a temporary λmax increase.
rows.note: The result is about condensation and Hessian sharpness; the learning rate is not described as above the stability limit.
rows.check: The recorded condensation and sharpness trends do not establish V5's threshold behavior; absence of a spike at an unspecified position relative to the stability threshold is not evidence against V5.

rows.subject: ReLU neural network
rows.operation_detail: Track condensed variance and λmax over early training at learning rate 0.05.
rows.measure: Time course of condensed variance and λmax; whether loss spikes occur.
rows.value: Loss spike observed; text states λmax and condensed variance show the same trend and both decrease during the same epoch, ignoring a temporary λmax increase.
rows.note: The result is about condensation and Hessian sharpness, not the wide-network recovery test in V5.
rows.check: The recorded sharpness–condensation correlation and spike occurrence do not establish the initial stability limit or prolonged threshold hovering with falling loss.

rows.subject: ReLU neural network
rows.operation_detail: Vary initialization parameter γ in the condensed regime and report average end-of-training condensed variance and λmax over 10 random seeds.
rows.measure: Condensed variance and λmax at end of training.
rows.value: As γ increases, both condensed variance and λmax exhibit a similar decaying trend; the text says γ > 1 is the condensed regime.
rows.note: The study reports averages over 10 random seeds but gives no uncertainty estimate.
rows.check: The initialization sweep measures terminal condensation and sharpness, rather than training speed, trainable depth, or the stability-recovery behavior.

rows.subject: ReLU neural network initialized in condensed regime
rows.operation_detail: Track condensed variance and λmax at early training for learning rates 0.03 and 0.05.
rows.measure: Condensed variance and λmax trajectories; loss-spike occurrence.
rows.value: Text says the results do not display similar trends: λmax begins very small, rises to a non-zero constant, while condensation increases and condensed variance decreases.
rows.note: This is an explicit initialization-condition exception in the paper's condensation/sharpness analysis; it does not test the listed initialization versions’ training outcomes.
rows.check: The exception concerns the relationship between condensation and sharpness. It does not challenge V4 or V5. Split the two learning-rate conditions if retained as separate experimental rows.

rows.subject: Sigmoid neural network
rows.size_stated: 500 hidden neurons, by the same settings as Fig. 8
rows.operation_detail: Vary learning rate and report end-of-training condensed variance and λmax.
rows.value: Text states condensed variance decreases as learning rate increases and λmax exhibits a decreasing trend mirroring it.
rows.note: The figure caption and text describe the correlation but do not report training classification error.
rows.check: Terminal condensation and sharpness do not measure a listed version. Appendix B.3 does not independently specify the claimed width of 500.

rows.subject: LeakyReLU neural network
rows.size_stated: 500 hidden neurons, by the same settings as Fig. 8
rows.operation_detail: Track condensed variance and λmax at early training at learning rates 0.01 and 0.04.
rows.measure: Condensed variance and λmax trajectories; loss-spike occurrence.
rows.value: Text states λmax consistently displays the same trend as condensed variance, irrespective of spike occurrence.
rows.note: No training classification-error outcome is reported.
rows.check: The sharpness–condensation correlation does not establish a listed effect. Split the two learning-rate conditions if retained; Appendix B.3 does not independently specify the claimed width of 500.

relationships.condition: Two-layer ReLU CNN on CIFAR10-1k with MSE and η = 0.1.
relationships.reason: R1 records loss increasing when sharpness exceeds 2/η and decreasing after sharpness drops below it; the authors identify this as edge-of-stability training.
relationships.display_finding: Loss increased when sharpness exceeded 2/η and decreased after sharpness dropped below it.

relationships.condition: Batch-normalized VGG-11 on 1,024 CIFAR-10 examples, η = 0.2 and 0.3.
relationships.reason: R2–R3 show recovering loss spikes with sharpness around the stability threshold, supporting V5's edge-of-stability component in these runs.
relationships.display_finding: Training recovered from loss spikes while sharpness remained around the stability threshold.

relationships.condition: Width-20 two-layer tanh FNN, full-batch gradient descent, η = 0.05.
relationships.reason: Based on text and Figure 2(a–c), absent from the rows: loss spikes during edge-of-stability training and decreases after sharpness returns below 2/η.
relationships.display_finding: Loss spiked during edge-of-stability training and decreased after sharpness returned below 2/η.
